entities.title: One pilot per browser
entities.summary: Each browser flies one ship; friends play together each on their own device, from the multiplayer page.
entities.context: Up to nine pilots can share a game, and online play already keeps several browsers in the same game.
entities.decision: Input turns every key, gamepad and touch button into one pilot's controls, LAUNCH starts a game for one, and a game with friends starts only from the multiplayer page, each pilot on their own device.
entities.rationale: One way to play together, with every pilot on their own screen and controls.

origin.description: Shatterbelt: one pilot per browser; groups play from the multiplayer page.

entities.title: Online games go on the public table
entities.summary: The host starts an online game with a seed from the server, each page names its own pilot, and the host submits the game with every name.
entities.context: Every page plays the whole game in lockstep (the lockstep decision recorded in Rally's src, where src/online.ts is the same file), so every page holds the same recording; the server replays a game from a seed it issued, once per seed.

options.title: Keep online games off the table
options.consequences: As Rally does: an online win is recorded nowhere.

options.title: Each page submits its own pilot
options.consequences: The seed is accepted once, so only the first page's pilot would get on.

options.title: The host submits for everyone
options.consequences: The pages exchange names after the game, and the host waits up to 120 s for them.

entities.decision: The host asks the server for the seed and sends its ticket in the start message. After the game every page sends its pilot's name; the lowest slot still in the room waits for every name or departure, submits the game with every name, and sends the results to the others.
entities.rationale: Online games count like any other, under one seed and one replay.
